narrative.overview:
The page is a printed singles chart, not a list of cards. A yellow masthead band carries the title, the strapline and the dateline, which leads with how long ago the chart was updated. Below it, a key strip gives the day's totals, a "Rank by" switch and a legend. Then a dense numbered sheet prints four columns per row: rank, days on, the repository, and stars today. Two inks do all the work: chart yellow and ink black on a white sheet. Hierarchy comes from condensed display numerals at very different sizes, heavy and hairline rules, and small reversed ink boxes that mark the facts worth a second look.

The chart ranks by stars today by default, so No. 1 is the day's top gain. GitHub's own order is one click away on the switch. Memory is the point of difference: the "Days on" column counts the days each repo has trended, and long runs print boxed in ink so staying power reads down the column at a glance.

Density is the point. On wide screens the sheet prints two columns at chart density, paired row by row, so a full chart reads like a page of a trade paper. On phones it collapses to one column without losing the rank, days-on and gain figures. The system follows the operating system's light and dark preference; the dark sheet keeps the yellow band.

There is no client script. Motion is one gesture: the NEW tag presses onto the sheet once on load.
keyCharacteristics: Chart yellow masthead band; white sheet; ink #111. Inside the chart, yellow marks NEW only.
Condensed Big Shoulders Display numerals for ranks, gains, days on and the dateline's age; Archivo for all text.
Ruled, not boxed: hairline row rules, a 3px rule under column heads and over the footer, a 6px rule under the masthead, a 2px ink divider between the desktop columns.
Reversed ink boxes for rank-worthy facts: runs of 4 days or more, the top gain in GitHub's order, the active rank order.
Tabular numerals across the whole page.

rules.name: The Yellow Means New Rule
rules.body: Inside the chart, a yellow mark means "first day on GitHub trending" and nothing else. The top gain, long runs and the active order print in ink, never yellow. The row hover wash is a tint, not a mark.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Everything prints in yellow and ink. Language swatches are the only other colours, because they are data from GitHub, not palette.

rules.name: The Numerals Are Display Rule
rules.body: Every number the reader ranks by (rank, days on, stars today, the dateline's age) sets in Big Shoulders Display. Counts inside running text (total stars, forks, the key's totals, the exact UTC time) stay in Archivo.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` applies to the whole page, so figures align down each column.

rules.name: The Label Names Data Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels name a column, a date or a data key. They never decorate a section heading.

rules.name: The Rules, Not Boxes Rule
rules.body: Separate content with rules of graded weight. Do not use cards, borders on four sides, or shadows. The only four-sided borders are the "Rank by" switch, which is a control, not a container.

rules.name: The Band Edge Rule
rules.body: In dark mode the 6px ink rule under the masthead does not print on the near-black sheet; the yellow band's own edge serves as the rule. Do not add a substitute rule colour to make it show.

dos: **Do** set every ranking figure (rank, days on, gain, the dateline's age) in Big Shoulders Display, at sizes that keep rank largest.
**Do** keep yellow inside the chart for NEW only.
**Do** mark rank-worthy facts with a reversed ink box: runs of 4 days or more, the top gain in GitHub's order, the active rank order.
**Do** separate rows with 1px hairlines and heads with a 3px ink rule.
**Do** keep the two-column chart in DOM order as two ordered lists, the second with `start`, and pair their rows with subgrid.
**Do** keep the stars-today sort stable, so ties keep GitHub's order.
**Do** cut descriptions at a word on the server, and keep the full text in `title`.
**Do** keep one underlined link per row: the repository name.
**Do** hide a homepage whole when it does not fit the one-line desktop meta row.
**Do** give every compact or visual-only figure a full screen-reader equivalent.
**Do** disable the NEW press under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** put repos in cards, rounded boxes or shadowed panels.
**Don't** add a third palette colour; language swatches are data, not palette.
**Don't** reverse the No. 1 row or mark the top gain in yellow.
**Don't** print avatars; the owner's name is enough.
**Don't** print a truncated fragment of a link; hide it whole.
**Don't** link a homepage that leads back to GitHub.
**Don't** put uppercase tracked labels above section headings as decoration.
**Don't** add motion beyond the NEW press.
